searchText: > Added a question regarding the spec: https://github.com/ethereum/stateless-ethereum-specs/issues/23 ``` <Tree> := 0xbb m:<Metadata> n:<Tree_Node(0)> {a tuple (m, n)} ``` Is the `0xbb` a canary or does it have any other use? In my understanding, no other use It would be nice to mention this in the spec as a note. I am sure others will ask about it. I've pushed a short discussion starter on the BLOCKHASH opcode's effect on Stateless Ethereum: https://ethresear.ch/t/the-curious-case-of-blockhash-and-stateless-ethereum/7304 Appreciate any feedback, even if it just means this is not a problem 😉 (Also copying this here as it discusses the witness.) Yeah, I noticed that when I was running witnesses (access to the previous block headers is needed as early as in the block 78000 on Mainnet). But so far, as Alexey say, we don’t want expand the scope too much. BTW, do you think it would more correct to call a radix tree with the radix 16 hexadecary rather than hexary? 🙂
